samples.summary: Canonical style design doc not updated for the new border write path
samples.evidence: `docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md` "Write Semantics" documents only `setStyle` ("Preserves explicit `false`/`0`/`""`", L63-67) and `setRangeStyle` (L69-77), and lists default-key pruning solely under "Range Patch Lifecycle" (L95-96, "default-only no-op keys are pruned"). The diff introduces a third per-cell write path (`Sheet.applyBorderPatch`, sheet.ts:3993) with its own pruning semantics — border presets no longer persist `bt/bl/br/bb: false` and can now delete a previously style-only cell — while the doc still says per-cell borders produced by `setRangeBorders` are simply stored on individual cells (L111-113). A reader of the doc would predict the old residue behavior. No design doc in the diff; the change ships only task docs under docs/tasks/active/, which are not the canonical subsystem doc.

Glob docs/design/**/*.md for a border-specific doc

samples.summary: applyBorderPatch re-implements setStyle's merge/compact/delete tail instead of sharing it
samples.evidence: Lines 4009-4034 duplicate almost exactly the body of `setStyle` (sheet.ts:3669-3685) — `store.get(anchor) || {}`, `mergeStylePatch`, `compactCell`, `isEmptyCell` -> `store.delete` else `store.set` — and the same compact/delete tail also appears in `clearCellStylesInRange` (sheet.ts:2004-2009). The genuinely new part is only the prune-the-touched-keys step (4003-4016); factoring the tail into one private `writeCellStyle(anchor, style)` would avoid a third copy of the persistence rule. This is a taste/structure preference, not a correctness claim.

samples.summary: Pruning is applied only to the border-preset path, leaving pre-existing `false` border residue unaddressed
samples.evidence: The issue frames the residue as data written into cells (`{"bt":false,...}`). `applyBorderPatch` only prunes the keys of the current patch on cells it touches, so documents already persisted with `bt/bl/br/bb: false` from before this change keep that residue unless a preset that touches those exact keys is re-applied (e.g. `top` only touches `bt`). The task doc's acceptance criterion is phrased about the round trip going forward, so this may be deliberately out of scope, but no migration/normalization is mentioned anywhere in the change or task docs.
